Let \(V=M_3(\mathbb F_2)\). First note that the graph distance is

\[
d(A,B)=\operatorname{rank}(A-B),
\]

since a rank \(r\) matrix is a sum of \(r\) rank-one matrices, and rank subadditivity gives the matching lower bound.

For a finite abelian group with translation-invariant kernel \(f(Z)=\operatorname{rank}(Z)^p\), the zero-sum quadratic form is diagonalized by the characters

\[
\chi_Y(Z)=(-1)^{\operatorname{tr}(Y^tZ)}.
\]

Thus \(p\)-negative type holds exactly when every nontrivial Fourier coefficient

\[
\widehat f(Y)=\sum_{Z\in V}\operatorname{rank}(Z)^p\chi_Y(Z)
\]

is \(\le 0\).

The coefficient depends only on \(s=\operatorname{rank}Y\). The rank counts in \(M_3(\mathbb F_2)\) are

\[
N_1=49,\qquad N_2=294,\qquad N_3=168.
\]

A direct count of the character sums over matrices of rank \(r=1,2,3\) gives:

\[
\begin{array}{c|ccc}
s & K_1(s)&K_2(s)&K_3(s)\\ \hline
1&17&6&-24\\
2&1&-10&8\\
3&-7&14&-8
\end{array}
\]

Hence the three nontrivial Fourier coefficients are

\[
\lambda_1(p)=17+6\cdot2^p-24\cdot3^p,
\]

\[
\lambda_2(p)=1-10\cdot2^p+8\cdot3^p,
\]

\[
\lambda_3(p)=-7+14\cdot2^p-8\cdot3^p.
\]

Here \(\lambda_1(p)<0\) for all \(p\ge0\), and \(\lambda_3(p)<0\) at the relevant threshold. The first coefficient to reach \(0\) is \(\lambda_2\). Since

\[
\lambda_2'(p)=-10(\log 2)2^p+8(\log 3)3^p>0
\]

for \(p\ge0\), it has a unique positive zero. Therefore

\[
\wp=\text{the unique positive solution of }
8\cdot3^p-10\cdot2^p+1=0.
\]

Numerically,

\[
\wp\approx 0.3489.
\]

At \(p=\wp\), equality occurs exactly on the characters with \(\operatorname{rank}Y=2\). There are \(294\) such characters, and they are linearly independent over \(\mathbb R\). Therefore

\[
\dim E=294.
\]

\[
\boxed{\left(\wp,294\right)}
\]

where \(\wp\) is the unique positive root of \(8\cdot3^\wp-10\cdot2^\wp+1=0\).
